content: Chlorpheniramine is an antihistamine that is prescribed to alleviate symptoms such as red, itchy, watery eyes, sneezing, and a runny nose caused by allergies, hay fever, or the common cold. It can also help relieve itching from insect bites, bee stings, poison ivy, and poison oak. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other uses, so consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Chlorpheniramine is available in various forms, including extended-release tablets and capsules, regular tablets and capsules, chewable tablets, liquid, and syrup, all of which are taken orally. It is typically taken every 4 to 6 hours or twice daily, in the morning and evening, as needed. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take chlorpheniramine exactly as directed, without exceeding or reducing the prescribed dose or frequency. Do not break, crush, or chew extended-release tablets, and do not open extended-release capsules; swallow them whole. Extended-release tablets or capsules should not be given to children under 12 years of age, and regular or chewable tablets or liquid should not be given to children under 6 years of age unless specifically directed by a doctor. Before taking chlorpheniramine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to it or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially those for colds, hay fever, allergies, depression, seizures, muscle relaxation, pain relief (narcotics), sedation, sleep aids, tranquilizers, or vitamins. Do not take chlorpheniramine if you have used an MAO inhibitor in the past two weeks. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had asthma, glaucoma, ulcers, diabetes, difficulty urinating (due to an enlarged prostate), heart disease, high blood pressure, seizures, or an overactive thyroid gland. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking chlorpheniramine, contact your doctor immediately. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking chlorpheniramine. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol can enhance the drowsiness caused by this medication, so avoid consuming alcohol while taking it. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Chlorpheniramine may cause side effects. Minor side effects include dry mouth, nose, and throat; upset stomach; headache; chest congestion; and diarrhea. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Severe side effects include vision problems, difficulty urinating, difficulty breathing, muscle weakness, prolonged drowsiness, unusual excitement (especially in children), dizziness, and skin rash. If you experience any of these severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or no longer needed medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Do not share this medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have any questions about refilling your prescription.
